_note: The published CKS curriculum, mapped onto this roadmap. The domains, weights and competency wording are the Linux Foundation's published curriculum, not exam content: the NDA covers what appears in the exam, and this is the public syllabus every training provider restates.

_status_meaning.covered: a checkpoint here addresses this competency directly
_status_meaning.partial: touched on, but the listed gap is not written up
_status_meaning.gap: nothing on this roadmap covers it yet

_coverage_caveat: The percentage is a rough weighting - full counts 1, partial counts 0.5 - and is a reading of the wording, not an official mapping. Treat it as a writing backlog, not as exam readiness.

competencies.text: Use Network security policies to restrict cluster level access
Use CIS benchmark to review the security configuration of Kubernetes components (etcd, kubelet, kubedns, kubeapi)
competencies.missing: kube-bench, reading a CIS report, and which findings actually matter on a managed cluster

competencies.text: Properly set up Ingress with TLS
competencies.missing: TLS termination on a Gateway listener, certificate issuance with cert-manager, and redirecting plaintext

competencies.text: Protect node metadata and endpoints
competencies.missing: blocking the cloud metadata endpoint from pods, and closing the kubelet read-only port

competencies.text: Verify platform binaries before deploying
competencies.missing: verifying Kubernetes release checksums and signatures specifically, as distinct from your own images

competencies.text: Use Role Based Access Controls to minimize exposure
Exercise caution in using service accounts e.g. disable defaults, minimize permissions on newly created ones
Restrict access to Kubernetes API
competencies.missing: anonymous auth, API server flags, and putting the control plane behind a network boundary

competencies.text: Upgrade Kubernetes to avoid vulnerabilities
competencies.missing: a real kubeadm upgrade, version skew rules, and draining nodes without breaking a PDB

competencies.text: Minimize host OS footprint (reduce attack surface)
competencies.missing: minimal node images, removing packages and services, and why a container-optimised OS changes the threat model

competencies.text: Using least-privilege identity and access management
competencies.missing: cloud IAM and workload identity, which is where this usually goes wrong - the in-cluster half is covered

competencies.text: Minimize external access to the network
Appropriately use kernel hardening tools such as AppArmor, seccomp
competencies.missing: writing and loading a seccomp profile, AppArmor profiles, and RuntimeDefault as a baseline

competencies.text: Use appropriate pod security standards
Manage Kubernetes secrets
Understand and implement isolation techniques (multi-tenancy, sandboxed containers, etc.)
competencies.missing: sandboxed runtimes - gVisor and Kata - and when the kernel boundary is not enough

competencies.text: Implement Pod-to-Pod encryption (Cilium, Istio)
competencies.missing: actually turning on WireGuard or IPsec in Cilium, or mTLS in Istio, rather than arguing about whether to

competencies.text: Minimize base image footprint
Understand your supply chain (e.g. SBOM, CI/CD, artifact repositories)
Secure your supply chain (permitted registries, sign and validate artifacts, etc.)
Perform static analysis of user workloads and container images (e.g. Kubesec, KubeLinter)
competencies.missing: kubesec, kube-linter and Trivy in CI, and which findings are worth failing a build over

competencies.text: Perform behavioral analytics to detect malicious activities
Detect threats within physical infrastructure, apps, networks, data, users and workloads
Investigate and identify phases of attack and bad actors within the environment
Ensure immutability of containers at runtime
competencies.missing: readOnlyRootFilesystem, dropping write access to the image layer, and enforcing it at admission

competencies.text: Use Kubernetes audit logs to monitor access
